Lockheed Martin’s Skunk Works has expanded its Vectis unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) program by building four additional aircraft as the team continues working toward the first flight in 2027.
Vectis is designed to evolve in response to mission requirements, while its ability to integrate with manned aircraft such as the F-35 will help extend the engagement envelope, enable new tactical capabilities, and provide greater flexibility against emerging threats.
The development team progressed from the initial UAV sketch to wind-tunnel testing in less than two months, completed the first digital model in six months, and built the first UAV in just eight months.

Denmark and Italy push forward on migration control.
The EU Parliament has voted to back new rules for return hubs outside Europe. This allows faster returns of rejected asylum seekers and irregular migrants to third countries, speeding up deportations and strengthening border management.
Led by efforts from Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen and Italy’s Giorgia Meloni, Europe is moving toward more pragmatic, effective migration policies.
